- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast slope to avoid overcorrection.
- If supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is low, model underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% downward buffer to forecast.
- When sentiment is mixed or bearish (≤0.33) and supply net is negative, model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average of true prices.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per event to reflect volatility dampening.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model may be underfitting; use 7-day rolling mean of true prices as baseline for correction.
